# Recording worksheet — one row per sound the game makes

**Generated by `scripts/sfx-manifest-doc.mjs` from the live registry.** Do
not hand-edit; re-run it instead. `docs/SFX_INVENTORY.md` remains the design
source of truth for how each sound should behave.

## How to add a sound

Drop a `.wav` into `public/assets/sfx/` named after the id, **dots replaced
by dashes**, plus any suffix you like:

```
crash.player.shard   ->   crash-player-shard.wav
                          crash-player-shard-a.wav
                          crash-player-shard-rice-02.wav
```

Nothing else is needed — no code change, no registry edit. Every file matching
an id is picked up automatically and **cycled round-robin**, so record as many
takes per action as you like; more takes means less repetition in bulk.

Then:

```bash
node scripts/prep-sfx.mjs public/assets/sfx/*.wav   # trim, normalise, 16-bit mono
node scripts/smoke/assets.mjs                       # check they are usable
```

To hear **only** your recordings with no synth underneath, open the pause menu
and press **Drafts ON** so it reads **WAV only**. Every id without a file goes
silent, and the counter beside it shows coverage.

## Reading the table

- **Tier** — mix priority. 1 never gets thinned under load; 3 is thinned first.
  Tier 1 is where recording effort pays off most.
- **Poly** — how many can sound at once. A low number with a high trigger rate
  means keep it SHORT (a voice holds its slot for the whole file).
- **Pos** — positional: panned and distance-attenuated, so record it dry and
  mono. Flat sounds are UI and can be wider.

Sounds already carrying at least one recorded take are marked ✅.

## Movement and materials

| | Sound id | File to create | Tier | Poly | ms | Pos | What it should sound like |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | `move.dent` | `move-dent-a.wav` | 3 | 4 | 140 | • | A single deforming knock. Softer than a break — nothing was destroyed. |
|  | `move.dent.recover` | `move-dent-recover-a.wav` | 3 | 3 | 180 | • | Reverse of the dent — a rubbery *boink* as the shape springs back. |
|  | `move.merge` | `move-merge-a.wav` | 3 | 3 | 150 | • | Two things becoming one — a short gluey suck with a soft landing. Very quiet; this fires all the time in a shard field. |
|  | `move.regenpop` | `move-regenpop-a.wav` | 3 | 3 | 200 | • | A gentle materialising pop — something came back. Friendly, not alarming. |
|  | `move.thrust` | `move-thrust-a.wav` | 2 | loop | **L** |  | Continuous engine rumble that **idles rather than switching on**. Throttle swells an already-running bed — gating the whole loop on `throttle > 0` snapped on and off with the input and read as jarring. Gain *and* cutoff move together (volume alone reads as a fader; timbre too reads as an engine working harder), both heavily smoothed. Must be *bland* — it plays constantly and any character in it becomes torture within five minutes. |
|  | `move.tilesnap` | `move-tilesnap-a.wav` | 3 | 2 | 260 | • | Crystallisation — fragments locking into a solid. A warm rising swell resolving on a soft thunk. Metal assembles constantly, so this fires in BULK: it must not stack into a whine. |

## Portals

| | Sound id | File to create | Tier | Poly | ms | Pos | What it should sound like |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | `portal.idle` | `portal-idle-a.wav` | 2 | loop | **L** | • | A LOW tonal hum that throbs. Two detuned sines beating slowly, plus a breath of heavily-lowpassed air — motion without brightness. Deliberately TONAL, against the station's broadband bed, so the two POIs are tellable apart by ear. **The first draft layered a 3 kHz Q3 noise shimmer on top and that was the whine players reported** — a ringing noise band held continuously is the most fatiguing thing audio can do. |
|  | `portal.open` | `portal-open-a.wav` | 2 | 2 | 800 | • | A rift tearing open at a distance — the transit sound heard from outside, shorter and darker. |
|  | `portal.transit` | `portal-transit-a.wav` | 1 | 1 | 1100 |  | Being pulled through: a rising whoosh that snaps into a brief silence, then a soft arrival bloom on the far side. Handles the whole cut — no separate arrival cue needed at the trigger site. |

|  | `poi.scrap` | `poi-scrap-a.wav` | 2 | 1 | 380 |  | Grinding destruction — a short shredder rasp resolving on a small chime for the credits. Audibly worse than selling, matching the 9% rate. |
|  | `poi.sell` | `poi-sell-a.wav` | 2 | 1 | 300 |  | The purchase figure inverted — descending, slightly duller. You gave something up. |
|  | `poi.station.idle` | `poi-station-idle-a.wav` | 2 | loop | **L** | • | LOW WHITE NOISE — a big machine idling. Broadband and pitchless, with a slow cutoff drift so it moves rather than sitting as flat hiss, and a faint mains hum underneath so it reads as machinery rather than weather. The deliberate opposite of the portal's tonal hum. |
|  | `poi.undock` | `poi-undock-a.wav` | 1 | 1 | 500 |  | Release and pressurise — the dock sound reversed, ending on a rising hiss. |
